Appellant has filed this appeal U/s.374(3) of Code of Criminal Procedure assailing the judgment of conviction and order of sentence passed in C.C.No.11169/2020 dated 31.05.2022 on the file of XXIII- Addl. Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru.

sentences.text: 2. Rank of the parties is referred to as per their ranks assigned before the trial court.

The facts of the case leading to this appeal may be summarized as under:
The Respondent is Complainant before the trial court.
This complainant and accused were friends since 13 years, accused was running his business under the name and style of "Varalakshmi Silk Sarees and Dresses" and

in the month of September 2009,
he approached the complainant for hand loan of Rs.10 lakhs for his financial commitments i.e., to clear debts and his legal necessities with a promise to repay the same within 5 years, accordingly, at his request complainant has paid an amount of Rs.7,75,000/- as hand loan to the accused, thereafter complainant demanded for repayment of loan amount in the month of 2 nd week of December 2014, at that time,
accused and his family members had executed an agreement of sale in favour of complainant pertaining to an immovable property bearing Sy. No.19/1 measuring 0.14.08 guntas and Sy. No.28/2 measuring 0.07.08 guntas Crl.A.No.467/2023 of land situated at Dodda Jala Amanikere village, Jala Hobli, Devanahalli Taluk,
Chikkaballapura District.

4. Further, accused towards repayment of the said amount and also accused has issued 2 post dated cheques bearing Nos.508452 and 508453 dated 11.03.2020 for sum of Rs.3,75,000/- and Rs.4 lakhs respectively in all Rs.7,75,000/- both the cheques are drawn on HDFC Bank, HRBR Layout Branch,
Kalyan Nagar, Bengaluru in favour of complainant with an assurance that the said cheques would be honoured on their presentation.

However, upon presentation of said cheques for encashment through his banker viz., Vijaya Bank, Moodalapalya Branch, Bengaluru on 11.03.2020, the same came to be dishonoured with an endorsement dated 13.03.2020 stating "Account closed".

Hence,
complainant got issued a legal notice and the same was duly served on name through R.P.A.D as well as by speed post on 20.03.2020 and 16.04.2020 respectively,
Despite, the same accused neither paid the cheques Crl.A.No.467/2023 amount nor replied to the legal notice.
After compliance of ingredients of section 138 of N.I. Act complaint is filed.
The trail court took cognizance and after Prashanth.

5. Before the trial court, accused appeared, got enlarged on bail.
The substance of accusation was recorded, he claimed trial.
The complainant got examined himself as Pw.1 and got marked in all 10 documents from Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.10 and closed her side.
The accused was examined U/s.313 of Code of Criminal Procedure.
On the other hand, accused has not chosen to cross-examin the P.W.1 and produce his side defence evidence.

Trial court, after hearing arguments on both sides and on appreciation of oral and documentary evidence, found accused committed an offence punishable U/s.138 of Negotiable Instrument Act, convicted and sentenced to pay a fine of Crl.A.No.467/2023 .8,00,000/- (Eight Lakhs rupees).
In default to undergo simple imprisonment for a period of 7 months.

6. Feeling aggrieved by the said judgment, accused person is appeared before this court urging the following grounds;
(a) The judgment and conviction passed by the Learned XXIII ACMM Court, Bangalore, passed in C.C.No.11169/2020 dated 31/05/2022 is totally perverse, illegal, unlawful and bad in law and therefore the same is liable to be set-aside by this Hon'ble court.
(b) The impugned judgment and conviction passed by the Trail court is contrary to facts, materials and evidence placed on records and as such the judgment and conviction is liable to be set-aside by this Hon'ble court.
(c) The learned Magistrate erred in placing much reliance upon the evidence of PW1 when his evidence is totally unbelievable, unacceptable and throws great doubt upon his credibility and reasonability.

Crl.A.No.467/2023 (d) That the learned Magistrate has further erred and failed to see that issuance of cheque is not at all an admitted fact and therefore without corroborating the evidence of PW1 and in the special circumstances of this case for want of corroboration ought to have rejected the un-believable story of PW1 and ought to have acquitted the appellant.
(e) The appellant further submitted that, on going through the entire records the following grounds were found:-
i) No appreciation of evidences ii) Debt of liability not established iii) No cogent evidence for due of such huge amount Prashanth.

viii) Uncontested (f) The learned Magistrate failed to appreciate this fact on defense side even though the complainant/ respondent has admitted the above mentioned facts during trial.

(o) The appellant submits that, due to lack of communication from earlier counsel, he was unable to know the status of the case and hence he could not prefer Crl.A.No.467/2023 appeal well in time and came to know about conclusion of his case recently when the police arrested and produced him before the court.
On these grounds, accused prayed to set aside the judgment dated 31.05.2022 in C.C.No.11169/2020 passed by the XXIII-Addl - Chief Metropolitan Magistrate Court at Bengaluru.

sentences.text: After registration of the appeal, notice was issued.
The respondent appeared through counsel.
The trial court records have been secured.
8. Heard arguments of respondent counsel and the same time, in-spite of giving sufficient opportunities, learned counsel for appellant has not chosen to canvas argument on behalf of the appellant.
Perused the written arguments of respondent side and the materials on record.

The points do arise for my consideration are as under;
1.
Whether appellant had sufficient cause for not preferring this appeal within the period of limitation ?

2. Whether cheques at Ex.P.1 and 2 were issued by the accused in favour of the complainant towards discharge of debt or liability as alleged in the complaint?
3. Whether trial court is correct in holding that, accused has committed offence punishable U/s.138 of Negotiable Instrument Act?
4. Whether there is legal infirmity in the impugned judgment, which requires interference of this court ?
5. What Order?

Perused the application filed u/s 142 of N.I. Act r/w Sec. 5 of Limitation Act and contents of affidavit, wherein it is sworn that during the trial stage accused was seriously sick and he was suffering from kidney problems and was undergoing treatment of dialysis,
he was unable to instruct his Advocate, subsequently case was adjourned for judgment, thereafter judgment of conviction passed against the accused , till date he is in judicial custody and taking treatment of dailysis.
In support of his contention regarding his health issues the appellant has produced the medical certificate, hence he could not give instructions to file Crl.A.No.467/2023 appeal on time.

The delay in preferring this appeal is for the aforesaid bonafide reasons and not intentional, if it is not condoned, there would be injustice to him, on the other hand if delay is condoned no hardship or prejudice would cause on the respondent.
12. On the contrary, the respondent / complainant has not filed objections to the I.A. for condonation of delay, hence, objections on above application is taken as nil.

13. Reasons assigned by the appellant to condone delay of 284 days in preferring this appeal appears to be genuine and satisfactory as he was suffering from kidney problems and under medical treatment and still he is in judicial custody and dialysis and under the facts and circumstances of the present case, this court opined that, it is just and proper to condone the delay of 284 days in preferring this criminal appeal to provide an opportunity to prosecute the petition.

However,
inconvenience caused Crl.A.No.467/2023 to the respondent / complainant has to be compensated suitably for not preferring the appeal well in time.
Hence this interim application deserves to be allowed.
Accordingly, point No.1 is answered in the Affirmative.
14. POINTS NO.2 AND 3:- These points are interrelated, hence they are taken up together for common discussion in order to avoid repetition of facts and evidence.

The learned counsel for the complainant canvassed in his written arguments by reiterating the facts submitted that, the trial court has rightly concluded that, the cheques in question issued towards discharge of debt or liability, except bald denials there was no specific defence of the accused before the trial court and accused has not chosen to cross-examine the PW.1 and to lead his side defence evidence in support of his case.

The learned counsel for respondent/ complainant brought to the court notice that the appellant is an habitual offender, involved in such or similar kind of criminal cases for the offences of cheating pending before Bagalakote, Gokarna, Davanagere and Koppala and he has been in judicial custody in some other cases, there is also a criminal case registered against him in Kunigal Police station in Crime No.198/2023 for the offence punishable u/sec 420 of I.P.C.
16.

It was further submitted that, as there are no sufficient funds in the account of the accused, in order to save himself from the clutches of the provisions of Section 138 of N.I.Act, this appeal is filed.
Therefore, he submits that, the judgment of the trial court is proper both in eye of law and on facts of the case and does not require any interference by this court.
Accordingly, learned counsel submits that, the appeal deserves dismissal.
In this background, this court has meticulously considered the complaint averments, documents placed by the complainant along with oral testimony and defence evidence placed by both parties.
Before proceedings further, it is relevant to reassert preposition of law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex court in connection with the cheque bounce cases.
The Hon'ble Court observed that, the presumptions U/s.139 of Negotiable Instrument Act is a presumption of law, it is not a presumption of fact.
This presumption has to be raised Crl.A.No.467/2023 by the court in all cases once the factum of dishonour is established.
The onus of proof to rebut this presumption lies on the accused.
The standard of rebuttal evidence depends on the facts and circumstances of each case.

The mere explanation is not enough to rebut this presumption of law, as reported in AIR 2001 SC 3897; Hiten P:. Dalal V/s. Bratinderanath Banerjee and (2006) 6 SCC 39; M.S.Narayan Menon alias Mani V/s.State of Kerala and another and ILR 2009 KAR 1633; Kumar Exports V/s. Sharma Carpets.
18.

sentences.text: As per the dictum of the Hon'ble Apex court, in a case of this nature, court shall consider the compliance of ingredients of the offence punishable U/s.138 of Negotiable Instrument Act.

Complainant has produced following documents;
1. Ex.
P.1 and 2- 2 cheques dated: 11.03.2020 2.
Ex.P.3- Bank Endorsements dated: 13.03.2020 Prashanth.

Ex. P.5 to 8 -Postal Receipts 5. Ex.P.9- Speed post Acknowledgment card 6. Ex.P.10- Track consignment.
Complaint filed on 04.06.2020.
Perusal of these documents show that, complainant has presented the cheques within validity period of 3 months.
Cheques returned unpaid with banker's memo for the reason "Account closed".
Within one month from the date of bank endorsements, legal notice has been issued.
After expiry of 15 days period to comply the terms of notice, present complaint filed within one month from the date of cause of action.
The accused has not disputed the signature present on the disputed cheques and also admitted that, cheques in question belong to the bank account maintained by him.

Therefore, it is claimed by the complainant that, legal presumptions enshrined U/s.139 and 118 of Negotiable Instrument Act could be raised in his Crl.A.No.467/2023 favour, which includes the existence of legally enforceable debt or liability.
19. It is worth to note that, the accused has not disputed nor denied the issuance of the subject cheque.
Hence, initial statutory presumption attached to the cheque as per Section 118(a) and 139 of N.I.Act has to be raised in favour of the complainant.

Section 139 of N.I.Act reads as under;
Sec.139. Presumption in favour of holder.--

It shall be presumed, unless the contrary is proved, that the holder of a cheque received the cheque of the nature referred to in section138 for the discharge,
in whole or in part, of any debt or other liability.
In the case on hand, it is clear that, signature on the cheque having been Prashanth.

8 admitted, a presumption shall be raised under Section 139 of the N.I.Act that the cheque was issued in discharge of debt or liability.

sentences.text: The question to be looked into is as to whether any probable defence was raised by the accused.
20 . The next point for consideration is whether the accused has placed cogent material on record sufficient to rebut the statutory presumption?
In a case of this nature, the defence of accused could be gathered from the reply Crl.A.No.467/2023 notice.
Plea of defence, suggestions and admissions in the cross-examination of Pw.1 and his witnesses.

The contentions taken in the reply notice acquires more credibility, as it is the first and foremost opportunity to the accused to place his defence by explaining the circumstances under which the disputed cheque reached the custody of the complainant.
Admittedly, accused has not issued reply notice, thereby, accused has forgone this maiden opportunity to put forth the defence/contentions.

21. It is the defence of the accused that, there was no such transaction between himself and the complainant there was no friendship amongst them, he has not at all issued any cheque in question to the complainant towards any liability, there was no legally enforceable debt, he was not served any legal notice, he do not know how the respondent came in possession of alleged cheques in question and misused the same.

It is the further case of accused that he was nto given sufficient opportunities by Crl.A.No.467/2023 the trial court, he is a businessman, the trial court without giving sufficient opportunities concluded the case.

22. In addition, according to the appellant there was no proper appreciation of the evidence by the trial court, debt of liability was not established, no cogent evidence was placed to substantiate that complainant has lent such a huge amount, the trial court failed to consider the denial of issuance of cheque in favour of the complainant by the accused.
It is relevant to note that, accused except denying the issuance of cheque in favour of the complainant, he has not taken any specific defence before the trial court.

As rightly pointed out by the trial court it is the statutory presumption raised in favour of the complainant that Exs.P.1 and P.2 cheques were issued by the accused for the payment of legally recoverable debt, though accused had ample opportunity, he has not taken any defence except making bald denial.
In this scenario, this Court has appreciated the evidence placed before the trial court to analyze the grounds raised by the accused person.
Section 106 of the Indian Evidence Act casts burden on the person who asserts the fact which is within his special knowledge.
The N.I.Act is special statute entitle the accused to rebut the presumption.
Except taking bare contention, accused person has not placed iota of evidence to show the previous transactions and repayment of the loan amount.
Therefore, this court is hesitant to believe this unsupported defence of the accused.

24. This proposition of law is laid down in the Hon'ble Apex court relied on the decision reported in,
2001 CRI.L.J 4745 (Supreme Court), between K.N. Beena Vs. Muniyappan, it is held that;
Prashanth. T.S vs Shankaregowda M.N on 10 February, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/48395057/
9

" Negotiable Instrument Act -S- 138, 139, 118- cheque dishonour complaint- Burden of proving that cheque had not been issued for any debt or liability - is on the accused - Denial/averments in reply by accused are not sufficient to Crl.A.No.467/2023 shift burden of proof on to the complainant- Accused has to prove in trail by leading cogent evidence that there was no debt or liability - setting aside conviction on basis of some formal evidence led by accused - Not proper. "
In this view of the matter, the formal evidence led by the accused is not sufficient to prove his defence.

25. From the discussions made supra, it is crystal clear that, complainant has placed convincing,
corroborative oral and documentary evidence to prove the loan transaction of Rs.10,00,000/- and issuance of two cheques for discharge of the said loan amount for an amount of Rs.3,75,000/- and Rs.4,00,000/- respectively towards principal amount.
Apart from that, complainant has also proved that, on presentation, said cheques were dishonoured for want of sufficient funds in the bank account maintained by the accused.
The service of legal notice is also proved.
The accused has not repaid the amount covered under the cheques till this day.
He has not Crl.A.No.467/2023 placed probable defence to dislodge the statutory presumptions raised in favour of the complainant.
Therefore, this court opined that, the complainant has successfully established the guilt of the accused punishable U/s.138 of Negotiable Instrument Act.
The learned trial Judge has considered all these aspects in proper perspective and rightly held that, accused has committed the offence punishable U/s.138 of N.I.Act.
Accordingly, Points No.2 and 3 under consideration are answered in the Affirmative.

26. POINT NO.4:- The complainant has placed cogent material to show compliance of all the ingredients of Section 138 of Negotiable Instrument Act, which envisages raising of statutory presumptions in favour of the complainant.
The accused is not successful in placing acceptable contentions to rebut the presumptions.
Thus, the complainant has proved the guilt of the accused punishable U/s.138 of Negotiable Instrument Act.

The trial court has assigned proper reasons in the impugned judgment of conviction as against the allegations made in the memorandum of appeal and proceeded to pass conviction and imposed sentence of fine amount.
No grounds are made out in the memorandum of appeal to interfere with the Impugned judgment of conviction.

28. So far as quantum of sentence is concerned, trial court has imposed sentence of fine directing the accused to pay fine of Rs.7,95,000/-(Rupees Seven Lakhs Ninety Five Thousand Only) to the complainant for dishonour of 2 cheques.

Out of fine amount of Rs.7,95,000/- (Rupees Seven Lakhs Ninety Five Thousand Only) Rs.7,90,000/-(Rupees Seven Lakhs Ninety Thousand Only) shall be paid to the complainant by way of compensation and Rs.5,000/- (Rupees Five Thousand Only) shall be paid to State exchequer.
In default of payment of fine amount, accused shall undergo simple imprisonment for a period of seven months.
Fine amount imposed is Crl.A.No.467/2023 within the Prashanth.

sentences.text: Accused failed to establish the fact that, sentence imposed is exhorbitant and excessive.
There is no merit in the appeal.
Order under appeal is sustainable in law.
Hence, interference of this court is not necessary.
Accordingly, point No.3 under consideration is answered in the Negative.
29. POINT NO.5:-
In view of findings on the above points No.1 to 4, this criminal appeal is devoid of merits and the same is liable to be dismissed by confirming impugned judgment of conviction and order of sentence.

Hence, this court proceed to pass the following:
ORDER I.A. No.I filed by the accused u/s 5 of the Limitation Act, is hereby allowed on payment of cost of Rs.1,000/-.
Consequently, delay of 284 days in  preferring the present appeal is hereby  condoned.

Chief Metropolitan Magistrate, Bengaluru

Appellant is directed to appear before the Trial Court to deposit the fine amount or to serve the default sentence.

The mere explanation is not enough to rebut this presumption of law, as reported in AIR 2001 SC 3897; Hiten P:. Dalal V/s. Bratinderanath Banerjee and (2006) 6 SCC 39; M.S.Narayan Menon alias Mani V/s.State of Kerala and another and ILR 2009 KAR 1633; Kumar Exports V/s. Sharma Carpets.
18.
Hence, initial statutory presumption attached to the cheque as per Section 118(a) and 139 of N.I.Act has to be raised in favour of the complainant.
It shall be presumed, unless the contrary is proved, that the holder of a cheque received the cheque of the nature referred to in section138 for the discharge,
in whole or in part, of any debt or other liability.
In so far as the payment of amount by the complainant in the context of cheque having been signed by the accused, the presumption for passing of consideration would arise as provided U/s.118(a) of N.I.Act, which reads as under;
Crl.A.No.467/2023 Sec.118. Presumptions as to negotiable instruments.--Until the contrary is proved, the following presumptions shall be made:
--
(a) of consideration:--that every negotiable instrument was made or drawn for consideration, and that every such instrument, when it has been accepted, indorsed,
negotiated or transferred, was accepted, indorsed, negotiated or transferred for consideration;
The above noted provisions are explicit to the effect that such presumptions would remain, until the contrary is proved.
21. It is the defence of the accused that, there was no such transaction between himself and the complainant there was no friendship amongst them, he has not at all issued any cheque in question to the complainant towards any liability, there was no legally enforceable debt, he was not served any legal notice, he do not know how the respondent came in possession of alleged cheques in question and misused the same.
As rightly pointed out by the trial court it is the statutory presumption raised in favour of the complainant that Exs.P.1 and P.2 cheques were issued by the accused for the payment of legally recoverable debt, though accused had ample opportunity, he has not taken any defence except making bald denial.
Section 106 of the Indian Evidence Act casts burden on the person who asserts the fact which is within his special knowledge.
The N.I.Act is special statute entitle the accused to rebut the presumption.
Except taking bare contention, accused person has not placed iota of evidence to show the previous transactions and repayment of the loan amount.
He has not Crl.A.No.467/2023 placed probable defence to dislodge the statutory presumptions raised in favour of the complainant.
26. POINT NO.4:- The complainant has placed cogent material to show compliance of all the ingredients of Section 138 of Negotiable Instrument Act, which envisages raising of statutory presumptions in favour of the complainant.
Thus, the complainant has proved the guilt of the accused punishable U/s.138 of Negotiable Instrument Act.
The trial court has assigned proper reasons in the impugned judgment of conviction as against the allegations made in the memorandum of appeal and proceeded to pass conviction and imposed sentence of fine amount.
No grounds are made out in the memorandum of appeal to interfere with the Impugned judgment of conviction.
Accused failed to establish the fact that, sentence imposed is exhorbitant and excessive.

28. So far as quantum of sentence is concerned, trial court has imposed sentence of fine directing the accused to pay fine of Rs.7,95,000/-(Rupees Seven Lakhs Ninety Five Thousand Only) to the complainant for dishonour of 2 cheques.
Out of fine amount of Rs.7,95,000/- (Rupees Seven Lakhs Ninety Five Thousand Only) Rs.7,90,000/-(Rupees Seven Lakhs Ninety Thousand Only) shall be paid to the complainant by way of compensation and Rs.5,000/- (Rupees Five Thousand Only) shall be paid to State exchequer.
In default of payment of fine amount, accused shall undergo simple imprisonment for a period of seven months.
Fine amount imposed is Crl.A.No.467/2023 within the Prashanth.
Accordingly, point No.3 under consideration is answered in the Negative.
29. POINT NO.5:-
In view of findings on the above points No.1 to 4, this criminal appeal is devoid of merits and the same is liable to be dismissed by confirming impugned judgment of conviction and order of sentence.
Hence, this court proceed to pass the following:
ORDER I.A. No.I filed by the accused u/s 5 of the Limitation Act, is hereby allowed on payment of cost of Rs.1,000/-.
Consequently, delay of 284 days in  preferring the present appeal is hereby  condoned.
Crl.A.No.467/2023 Further this Criminal Appeal U/s.374(3) of Code of Criminal Procedure filed by the appellant is dismissed.
Consequently, the judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 31.05.2022 passed in C.C.No.11169/2020 on the file of XXIII-Addl.
is confirmed.
Appellant is directed to appear before the Trial Court to deposit the fine amount or to serve the default sentence.
